html:
Yasser Arafat was the leader of the Palestinian national movement for four decades. He chaired the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) from 1969 to 2004.

Born in Cairo to Palestinian parents, he was a student activist when the 1948 war and the Nakba scattered Palestinians across the region. In the late 1950s he helped found Fatah, which turned to guerrilla attacks on Israel.

  • After the 1967 war Fatah took over the PLO.
  • Fighting with Jordan in 1970 drove the PLO to Lebanon, and Israel's invasion in 1982 drove it to Tunis.
  • Groups under the PLO carried out hijackings and attacks on civilians.

In 1988 he accepted Israel's right to exist, and in 1993 he signed the Oslo Accords with Yitzhak Rabin. He returned to Gaza to head the new Palestinian Authority and shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 1994. Peace talks failed in 2000, the second intifada broke out, and Israel kept him besieged in Ramallah until he fell ill and died in France.
